To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the richness of waterbirds in 19 wetland habitats in southwestern Ontario, were related to wetland size and isolation, and to the presence of roads and forest in the surrounding landscape.

(1) wetland size and isolation from other wetlands were the most important variables in determining species richness of waterbirds in urban and near-urbanscapes; (2) the number of roads and forest cover adjacent to wetlands were the second most important variables in predicting species richness of waterbird guilds; and (3) species richness of water bird guilds in the urban and near-urbscapes were best explained using log-linear models.

understanding and predicting the effects of habitat fragmentation on waterbird communities.
the effects of habitat size and isolation on waterbird species richness and abundance.
the conservation of waterbirds in urban and near- urban environments.
